## Who he is

Raghav Mahajan is a junior SOC analyst and web developer in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. He works in physical security (site supervision in corporate security, and loss prevention and screening) while building a cybersecurity career through certifications and a four-node home SOC lab. He builds secure websites and web apps for small businesses as a freelance developer. He also publishes the Blue Team Brief, a cybersecurity newsletter.

Education: Diploma in Computer Software Engineering (Digital Media and IT program) from NAIT (Northern Alberta Institute of Technology), Edmonton, 2022 to 2024.

Work authorization: Canadian post-graduation work permit (PGWP), an open work permit; no sponsorship required. Open to SOC analyst and IT support roles across Canada, including remote work and relocation. He also understands Hindi, Punjabi and Urdu.

## Cybersecurity and SOC work

Focus areas: SOC analysis and security operations, blue team monitoring and detection, incident response practice, SIEM operations, log analysis, network security and packet analysis, Active Directory and Windows Server administration, Linux system administration, Python security automation, and web application security.

Featured investigation:
- LAB-001, SSH Brute Force Detection: https://www.raghv.dev/investigations/lab-001-ssh-brute-force
  A Wazuh detection captured in the home lab on Oct 14, 2026. A login attempt against a non-existent user fired Wazuh rule 5710, and the repeated attempts fired rule 5712 (SSH brute force attack detected) on DC-01, the lab domain controller. The write-up covers the captured telemetry, what the two rules mean, the order of events, and the limits of a single lab capture. Every alert came from an attack Raghav ran himself against his own lab.

Cybersecurity page: https://www.raghv.dev/cybersecurity (SOC skills, MITRE ATT&CK detection coverage, lab questions and answers)

### The home SOC lab

A four-node home lab used for detection practice, with 50+ documented attack simulations, each with a written report, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. The stack:
- Wazuh (SIEM, running in Docker): agents on the lab nodes, custom rules and decoders, alert triage
- Splunk: SPL queries, dashboards and weekly hunts (lab use)
- Windows Server 2022 with Active Directory: domain controller DC-01, account and group policy work
- Ubuntu and Kali Linux nodes: targets and the attack platform (password spraying, Kerberoasting, DNS tunnelling, suspicious PowerShell)
- Wireshark and tcpdump: packet capture and analysis
- Docker: the lab services run as containers and can be rebuilt quickly

Lab write-ups: https://www.raghv.dev/blog/docker-soc-lab and https://www.raghv.dev/blog/wazuh-siem-home-lab
